title: Gukesh escapes time crisis to draw world chess championship opener with Sindarov
content: Opening game ends in draw by repetition Defending champion plays white in Game 2 Read our move-by-move report of Game 1 Sindarov: ‘I can’t play games just for fun’ Indian chess star Gukesh Dommaraju held off Javokhir Sindarov amid a mounting time crisis on Tuesday, drawing the opening game of their eagerly awaited $2.5m world title match in 38 moves at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in the picturesque Geneva suburb of Cologny. After spending more than 36 minutes on a single move and much of the afternoon racing against the clock, the defending champion said the time he invested early helped him play faster as a drawish position sharpened and his minutes dwindled opposite the in-form Uzbek challenger. “When I got into the time trouble, I’d already thought about the next few moves,” Gukesh said. “And then the moves after that were pretty easy.”
summary: Gukesh escapes time crisis to draw world chess championship opener with Sindarov.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Gul scores as Galatasaray beat Aston Villa in Champions League
content:
Aston Villa suffered a Champions League defeat at Galatasaray in Istanbul, marking their sixth consecutive match without a win in all competitions. The Turkish hosts secured the victory with a 77th-minute goal from substitute Deniz Gul, who was the game’s first effort on target. Gul sustained a facial injury during the match, requiring a bandage after receiving a boot to the face from Nicolas Jackson.

The loss was Villa’s third trip to Istanbul this calendar year, contrasting sharply with their previous visits to Fenerbahce in January and their Europa League triumph at Besiktas Park in May. Manager Unai Emery noted that the poor pitch conditions, which began deteriorating during warm-ups, were equal for both teams. Despite John McGinn’s frustration with the surface after a through ball went awry, the article states that no one from Villa could blame the defeat on the playing conditions. Galatasaray maintained their strong home form, while Villa made four changes from their recent stalemate with Sunderland.
summary: Deniz Gul scored the only goal in the 77th minute to secure a victory for Galatasaray over Aston Villa. This result extended Aston Villa's winless run to six matches in all competitions.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Rayan Cherki equalizer denies Manchester City win against Napoli
content:
Manchester City’s struggles continued as they drew with Napoli, a result that highlighted the team’s ongoing difficulties despite a late surge in energy. The match featured a debut for City’s new rust-colored kit, though the performance largely reflected a familiar frustration before the home side shook off their torpor in the closing stages.

Rayan Cherki provided a crucial equalizer, scoring with an angled shot that passed Vanja Milinkovic-Savic after an otherwise fruitless evening of effort. This goal denied Napoli a victory and ended the prospect of a triumphant return to the Etihad for Kevin De Bruyne.

Although Napoli, currently eighth in Serie A, were described as lacking their previous intensity, City’s inability to maintain a lead meant they could not secure a win. The match served as a snapshot of the team’s autumn challenges, with the final scoreline offering only partial relief from their defensive vulnerabilities.
summary: Rayan Cherki scored an equalizer to prevent Manchester City from defeating Napoli in a match that highlighted the visitors' ongoing struggles. The result ended the prospect of a triumphant return to the Etihad for Kevin De Bruyne, who played in the game.

title: Bayern hold 'constructive' talks over Musiala's health
content: Bayern Munich sporting director Max Eberl stated that the club is solely focused on recovering Jamal Musiala from injury. Eberl insisted that the team is not interested in comments regarding Musiala's contract, noting that recent discussions about the player's health have been constructive.
summary: Bayern Munich are only focused on getting Jamal Musiala back from injury and not interested in the comments made regarding his contract, the club's sporting director Max Eberl insists.

content: A new The Economist/YouGov poll reveals that 28 percent of Americans have “very little” faith in the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). The survey found that 44 percent of respondents expressed “some” confidence in the agency, while 19 percent reported having “quite a lot” of confidence.

content: The Federal Aviation Administration issued a ground stop at Chicago’s O’Hare International Airport on Tuesday, marking the second brief flight pause in two days. The restriction, which remained in effect until 4:15 p.m. local time, was implemented due to an equipment outage affecting a ground surveillance radar and tracking system.

title: England coastal areas to receive over £11m for 12 council‑led projects
content:
England’s government has announced more than £11 million in new funding to help coastal communities adapt to rising seas and erosion accelerated by climate breakdown. The money will be distributed across 12 council‑led projects aimed at detecting coastal change earlier and assisting local planning.

Among the supported schemes are laser‑equipped drone surveys, sand dune restoration, and the relocation of roads inland. These initiatives are intended to give seaside communities tools to monitor erosion and to prepare for its impacts.
summary: More than £11 million will be shared among 12 council‑led projects in England’s seaside communities. The projects, such as laser‑equipped drone surveys, sand dune restoration and moving roads inland, aim to detect coastal change earlier and help communities plan for rising seas and accelerated erosion.

title: 120 climate scientists urge US lawmakers to reject Baaja permitting bill
content:
More than 120 climate scientists have signed an open letter urging US House members to reject the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, commonly known as Baaja. The researchers, who include Earth and social sciences experts, stated they have “deep concern” that the legislation weakens environmental laws. They further argued that the bill locks in new fossil fuel projects without recourse and results in only minor reductions to planet-heating emissions.

The letter warns that Baaja, which is intended to expedite energy and infrastructure projects, will cause irreversible climate harm. This call for a "no" vote comes amid a growing backlash against the sweeping permitting bill, which aims to accelerate the construction of energy projects, datacenters, and other infrastructure.
summary: More than 120 climate scientists sent an open letter to House members urging them to vote against the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. The researchers stated that the bill weakens environmental laws and locks in new fossil fuel projects without recourse.
author: Guardian Environment

title: California king tides flood San Francisco low-lying areas
content:
California is experiencing record-high November tides that have caused flooding in low-lying areas along the coast. In San Francisco, flood waters rushed over the bayfront Embarcadero in the city’s tourist district, while flooded roadways were reported from San Rafael to Redwood Shores. These events occurred despite clear skies, and monthly tide records were set across the city, with some expected to reach even higher levels tomorrow.

The extreme tides have also prompted an evacuation of one community in northern California. Local residents and media outlets shared images documenting the widespread impact of the water on roadways and public spaces.
summary: Record-high November tides caused flooding in San Francisco's Embarcadero and other coastal areas. One community in northern California was evacuated due to the high water levels.
author: Guardian Environment

title: b/tsDMARD use patterns in rheumatoid arthritis linked to genetic associations
content: A study published online Nov. 20 in Arthritis & Rheumatology reports that common patterns of biologic and targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (b/tsDMARD) use exist among patients with rheumatoid arthritis. The research indicates that these specific usage patterns are associated with underlying genetic associations.
summary: A study found that common patterns of biologic and targeted synthetic DMARD use among rheumatoid arthritis patients are associated with underlying genetic factors. The research was published online in Arthritis & Rheumatology on November 20.

content: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Nelkarmi (neladalkib), a kinase inhibitor, for adults with locally advanced or metastatic ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer who have received prior treatment. The approval was granted to Nuvalent and GSK.

content: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved the combination of bezuclastinib and sunitinib as a second-line therapy for adults with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) following first-line imatinib treatment. This decision was based on phase 3 PEAK study data led by Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, which demonstrated that the combination outperformed standard sunitinib monotherapy.
summary: The FDA approved the combination of bezuclastinib and sunitinib as a second-line treatment for adults with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors. content: A new study led by University of Michigan researchers found that state laws limiting prior authorization requirements for opioid use disorder medications were associated with increased buprenorphine use in Medicaid. This association was observed only in states where such prior authorization requirements had frequently acted as barriers to access.
summary: State laws limiting prior authorization for opioid use disorder medications were linked to higher buprenorphine use in Medicaid. The effect was seen only in states where prior authorization requirements were frequent barriers to access, according to a University of Michigan study.

content: Adolescence is often described as a turbulent period of life marked by growing independence, changing social relationships and unpredictable shifts in behavior. Researchers note that tweens' and teens' behavioral changes reflect a brain that is still actively developing. Yet scientists know surprisingly little about the neural mechanisms that shape social behavior during this critical stage of life.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologizes to staff for code of conduct violations
content:
Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang apologized to employees on Tuesday, saying he had caused “tumult” at the company. In a livestream reviewed by the New York Times, Huang acknowledged that he violated Nvidia’s code of conduct by engaging in extramarital affairs, describing his actions as “terrible mistakes” that hurt his wife Lori, his children and the staff.

He also rejected media reports that former President Donald Trump played a role in Huang’s return to the chief‑executive post, stating that those claims were inaccurate.
summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, apologized to employees, saying he made terrible mistakes and hurt his family and staff. He acknowledged violating the company’s code of conduct by having extramarital affairs and denied that Donald Trump was instrumental in his reinstatement as chief executive.

title: Underwater robots reveal first salp species known to live exclusively in deep sea
content:
Larry Madin, deputy director emeritus at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution and an MBARI adjunct, recently published a detailed description of the glass salp (Vitreosalpa gemini) in the journal Marine Biodiversity. This striking species is the first salp known to live exclusively in the deep sea. Madin utilized specimens and data collected by MBARI’s advanced underwater robots to document the animal, which researchers had first observed in the deep waters of Monterey Bay more than 20 years ago.

Salps are barrel-shaped gelatinous animals that play an important role in ocean ecosystems. The new publication provides a comprehensive account of this previously unfamiliar species, highlighting its unique adaptation to deep-sea habitats.
summary: Salps are barrel-shaped gelatinous animals that play an important role in ocean ecosystems. More than 20 years ago, researchers observed an unfamiliar salp in the deep waters of Monterey Bay.
author: Phys.org

title: Laser light maps electron accumulation in atomically thin semiconductor stacks
content:
A multi-institutional team in Japan has demonstrated that shining laser light on stacked semiconductors reveals where electrons accumulate within atomically thin stacks. While stacking these materials, which power devices such as phones and computers, allows for quicker signal movement with less energy, the specific mechanisms of electron movement had remained unclear. This optical approach provides a method to visualize these internal processes.

The researchers stated that this technique could inform the development of more efficient, low-power electronics. By elucidating how electrons move within the semiconductor stacks, the study offers new insights into optimizing the performance of next-generation electronic components.
summary: Stacking semiconductors enables quicker signal movement with less energy. A multi‑institutional team in Japan used laser light to reveal how electrons move in the stack, a method that could help develop more efficient, low‑power electronics, the researchers said.

content: Computers have steadily become faster and more powerful over the past decades. Avik Dutt, an assistant professor of mechanical engineering at the University of Maryland, proposes a dramatic new leap forward that would be driven by the quantum properties of light.

title: Scientists Achieve First Total Synthesis of Antitussive Alkaloid Neotuberostemonine
content:
Researchers have accomplished the first total synthesis of neotuberostemonine, a complex plant‑derived alkaloid noted for its antitussive activity. The breakthrough also included the synthesis of neostenine and the putative structure of tuberostemonine L, compounds that had remained elusive for nearly three decades.

The study further revealed that the nearly planar geometry of the alkaloids’ nitrogen atoms contributes to their oxidative instability. These insights provide new synthetic strategies for natural‑product chemistry and may inform future drug‑discovery efforts.
summary: Researchers have achieved the first total synthesis of the plant-derived alkaloid Neotuberostemonine, known for its antitussive activity. The study also synthesized neostenine, proposed the structure of tuberostemonine L, and showed that the nearly planar geometry of nitrogen atoms contributes to the alkaloids' oxidative instability, providing new synthetic strategies.

title: Depression Linked to Tau Protein Accumulation in Older Adults
content:
Scientists have found a link between accumulating tau protein, a hallmark of Alzheimer's disease, and worsening depressive symptoms in older adults. This association was observed in individuals who still possessed normal memory and thinking abilities. The research indicates that the rate of tau buildup in the brain corresponds with the speed at which depressive symptoms increase.

These findings suggest that mood changes may serve as an early warning sign of Alzheimer's disease, potentially emerging before any cognitive decline is detected.
summary: Scientists found that accumulating tau protein was linked to worsening depressive symptoms in older adults with normal memory and thinking abilities. The faster tau built up, the faster depressive symptoms increased, indicating mood changes may appear before cognitive decline.

title: New materials crawl, walk, and dig like living creatures using internal energy
content: Scientists have created materials that can crawl, walk, and dig by using their own internal energy, offering a potential foundation for autonomous soft robots. In testing, they found that increasing the activity of individual components can paradoxically reduce the overall responsiveness of the material, challenging a long‑standing engineering principle.
summary: Scientists have developed materials that can crawl, walk, and dig using their own internal energy, potentially enabling new autonomous soft robots. They also found that increasing component activity can paradoxically make the entire material less responsive.

content: MIT scientists report that tiny black holes from the Big Bang could slowly consume stars from the inside, leading to spectacular explosions visible across galaxies. Detecting these events may confirm the existence of primordial black holes and help resolve the mystery of dark matter.
summary: MIT scientists discovered that tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang could slowly devour stars from within, eventually triggering spectacular explosions visible across galaxies. Detecting these unusual cosmic events could reveal the existence of primordial black holes and help solve the mystery of dark matter.

title: Earth’s ancient oceans may have fooled scientists about its oxygen history
content: A new analysis proposes that Earth’s transition from an oxygen-poor environment to one supporting complex life occurred in three distinct atmospheric stages. The study indicates that the oceans lagged behind this atmospheric accumulation, potentially taking millions or even hundreds of millions of years to reach comparable oxygen levels.
summary: Earth’s ancient oceans may have fooled scientists about its oxygen history.

title: Nasal drops restore memory and halt Alzheimer’s-like decline in mice
content:
A new nasal treatment has restored youthful learning and memory in aging mice and prevented severe cognitive decline in mice with Alzheimer’s-like disease. Developed using technology similar to COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, the nose drops stimulate the production of a brain-protecting protein that strengthens neurons and supports memory.

The treatment preserved brain function without removing Alzheimer’s-associated plaques, suggesting a distinct approach to combating cognitive decline.
summary: The nasal treatment restored youthful learning and memory in aging mice and prevented severe cognitive decline in mice with Alzheimer’s-like disease. It works by stimulating production of a brain‑protecting protein and preserves brain function without removing Alzheimer’s plaques.

title: NASA’s Northrop Grumman CRS-25 Mission to Deliver 11,000 Pounds of Supplies to ISS
content:
NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 (CRS‑25) mission will deliver approximately 11,000 pounds of science and supplies to the International Space Station (ISS). The cargo is carried on the company’s Cygnus XL spacecraft, the larger, more cargo‑capable version of its solar‑powered spacecraft. Cygnus XL will launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.

After launch, the Cygnus XL will rendezvous with the ISS. Astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney will be on duty during the spacecraft’s approach. Watkins will operate the Canadarm2 robotic arm, while Delaney will monitor the arrival of Cygnus. Once captured, ground controllers will robotically install the spacecraft to the Unity module’s Earth‑facing port for cargo unloading.

The cargo package includes crew supplies such as food, blankets, hatch seal covers, a modified toilet pretreat hose, Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer spacewalk tools, and batteries for the Anomaly Gas Analyzer. In addition to these items, Cygnus will carry several experiments aimed at advancing medical research and life‑support technologies for future missions. The experiments include Cardinal Muscle 2.0, which tests potential therapeutics on engineered muscle tissue to address age‑related muscle loss; DNA Nano Therapeutics‑Mission 2, which manufactures DNA‑inspired nanoparticles for targeted drug delivery; the Active Radiation Environment Sensor (ARES), which monitors radiation in habitable spacecraft environments; Encapsulate‑1, which grows patient‑derived tumor samples to study metastasis; and OHALO III, a plant‑growth facility that validates water delivery and crop production for long‑duration missions. A technology demonstration, IN‑Space (JOINS), will perform autonomous robotic welding in the Bishop Airlock, testing laser beam welding and friction stir welding on aluminum and stainless‑steel.

The mission’s payload and experiments support NASA’s ongoing research into health, safety, and life‑support systems for crewed spaceflight. For more information on NASA’s work in low Earth orbit, visit https://www.nasa.gov/international-space-station.
summary: NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission, or Northrop Grumman CRS-25, will deliver about 11,000 pounds of science and supplies to the International Space Station. The mission will be the third flight of the company’s Cygnus XL, the larger, more cargo-capable version of the company’s solar-powered spacecraft.
author: NASA News

title: Kilonova Catcher lets amateur astronomers help track neutron‑star collisions
content:
NASA’s Kilonova Catcher invites amateur astronomers to help track some of the universe’s most fleeting fireworks. When two neutron stars collide, they can release a brief flash of light called a kilonova. These events, which fade within days, are responsible for forging much of the universe’s gold, platinum and other heavy elements. Because no single observatory can monitor the entire sky, the Kilonova Catcher network relies on volunteers with telescopes and cameras to respond quickly to alerts from gravitational‑wave detectors or space telescopes.

The network operates as a rapid‑response system. When a gravitational‑wave detector or a space‑based instrument issues an alert, participants point their telescopes at the indicated sky region to locate and follow the fading light. The same system also follows up on gamma‑ray bursts, the most powerful explosions in the universe, and other short‑lived cosmic events whenever an opportunity arises.

More than 150 members across several continents have joined the effort. Their observations have already contributed to more than 64 official reports shared through NASA’s General Coordinates Network, the real‑time system scientists use to exchange discoveries. Volunteers’ data have been credited as authors in peer‑reviewed scientific papers. In addition, Kilonova Catcher participants joined NASA’s lunar Impact Flash! Project campaign during the Artemis II mission, recording the tiny flashes of light produced when meteoroids strike the Moon.

The project is preparing to help follow up thousands of new alerts from NASA’s forthcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. “Here at Kilonova Catcher, by chasing the light from gravitational‑wave events, we’re seeing how a single collision reaches across the universe,” said Cristina Andrade, Kilonova Catcher head of operations at the Minnesota Institute for Astrophysics. “The observatories that make this possible will produce an unprecedented amount of data. We need more human minds, more people with their eyes on the sky and on the data, both literally and figuratively. And more importantly, we need more people to realize they are capable of great feats of science, regardless of their background.”

The project is co‑led by Andrade and Principal Investigator Dr. Damien Turpin, a researcher at the French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission (CEA). Turpin noted, “I am inspired by the expertise and drive of our amateur astronomers. They are always digging for more information and pushing the limits of their understanding. This science could not be done without their contributions.” To join, visit https://kilonovacatcher.in2p3.fr/ or email kilonovacatcher@gmail.com. Anyone with access to a telescope equipped with a camera can participate.
summary: Explore This Section Science Citizen Science Amateur Astronomer? Be a… Overview Resources Opportunities Citizen Science Highlights About Science Activation Neutron stars are the ultra-dense, city-sized leftovers of dead stars.

title: Mason: Lightweight Postgres read‑replica built on columnar storage
content:
Mason is an open-source, lightweight read-replica for PostgreSQL that utilizes DuckDB’s columnar compute engine. The developers describe it as a drop-in replacement that offers high speed while maintaining a PostgreSQL-like interface. The project originated from an attempt to use ClickHouse to accelerate analytics queries on PostgreSQL databases. However, the team found that ClickHouse required significant learning for engine optimization and had SQL syntax that differed too greatly from PostgreSQL for their ad-hoc workloads.

To find a suitable alternative, the team evaluated several tools, dismissing options like pg_mooncake, pg_duckdb, Materialize, RisingWave, ReadySet, Firebolt, Redshift, and AlloyDB based on factors such as project status, licensing, or the need to know query shapes in advance. They shortlisted three candidates: pg_clickhouse, cedarDB, and DuckDB. The team selected DuckDB for its open-source license, which allowed them to modify the engine to achieve better PostgreSQL SQL parity.

To evaluate performance, the developers conducted an experiment using 5,410 hand-written queries from 159 real PostgreSQL databases. These queries were selected because they had previously executed slowly. The team generated synthetic data based on the schemas of those 159 databases to create local test environments. They then ran each query against PostgreSQL and the three shortlisted tools to compare results, defining “matched” as returning the exact same result as PostgreSQL, “refused” as returning an error, and “wrong” as returning incorrect results.

The initial benchmark results showed that pg_clickhouse matched PostgreSQL 59.4% of the time, refused 39.9% of queries, and produced wrong results 0.8% of the time. cedarDB matched PostgreSQL 88.1% of the time, refused 8% of queries, and was wrong 3.9% of the time. DuckDB matched PostgreSQL 84.1% of the time, refused 14.3% of queries, and was wrong 1.6% of the time. The team considered PostgreSQL the golden source of truth for these comparisons.

Building on DuckDB, the team developed Mason to address the remaining compatibility gaps. Mason now matches PostgreSQL on 96% of the original 5,410 queries, as well as hundreds of additional queries tested with tools including Metabase, Grafana, Superset, DBeaver, and Trevor. For the remaining 4% of queries, Mason provides a clear error message explaining how to rewrite the SQL. The developers are seeking feedback on the tool’s usefulness and potential improvements.
summary: Mason is an open‑source drop‑in replacement for a Postgres read‑replica that uses DuckDB’s columnar compute engine and matches 96 % of the 5,410 queries tested. It was chosen after evaluating alternatives such as pg_clickhouse, cedarDB, and ClickHouse, and is designed to provide near‑Postgres SQL compatibility while remaining lightweight and cloud‑provider agnostic.

title: Launch HN: Versine (YC F26) – MCP to send and receive money
content: Hey HN, we’re Harshith, Param, and Vishnu and we're building Versine ( https://versine. Com ). Versine lets you send and request money just by talking or texting with your AI (think Venmo with an MCP). We’re software engineers who have worked on distributed systems at Stripe, Databricks, and Amazon. Versine is an MCP that sits in front of a wallet with a balance. With it, your agent can do things like: - Send money to someone with your approval (via passkey in our app) - Send and request money to/from up to 100 people at once - Send money to people without a Versine account (they cash out to their bank in 2 mins) - Pay people without your explicit approval to trusted contacts (you can set this) Here’s a demo: https://youtube. Com/shorts/Q9X7zioEqi0 We started working on this because assistants are frustratingly hands-off when it comes to finance and money movement. You can have your assistant go through a receipt and map out all the amounts owed taking care of splitting the subtotal, taxes, tips, but at the end of it the assistant hands back work to you when you have to go out and make the Venmo transfer. Our current solution is oriented towards power users: those who want to automate everything through their agent use us to split dinners, group trips, or settle poker ledgers. We see ourselves unlocking more value for the general consumer as 1. More people turn into power users of agents, and 2. We expand to a more complete banking solution: deposits, transfers, wires, everything you can (and more) do with your bank offered as an MCP. Behind the scenes, each user has a self-custodial stablecoin wallet storing USDC on Base. With self-custodial wallets, users own their keys, meaning money can’t be sent without their approval. Interestingly, we were almost forced into this solution because we had around 4 weeks to build this product (after a pivot), and traditional fiat with a partner bank would have caused far too many regulatory and compliance slowdowns. Because of that, the only fast option that remained was using stablecoin wallets. It also ensures we aren't a Money Services Business (MSB) since we don’t hold control or access to the user’s funds. Each call to the wallet creates what we call one-time or recurring standing permissions. For a one-time payment, your agent makes an MCP call, and you receive a notification in our mobile app. Once you swipe up in the app and approve with a passkey (or your device’s biometric method), we create a one-time permission that instructs your wallet to send $X to your recipient’s address. Trusted contacts let your agent send money to people that you’ve previously authorized without explicit passkey approval. Generally, these are people that you’d trust to send your money back even if your agent made a mistake. We’re also able to support sending money to someone off Versine using claim forwarding, where the user authorizes us to forward a specific amount to a future address (which we create once we verify a recipient's OTP). Param worked on scaling vector search at Databricks and harness evals at Glean. Harshith worked on core Stripe Connect fee-processing infrastructure and built an AWS Fargate autoscaler at Amazon. Vishnu worked on intent-based agent testing infrastructure at Amazon. None of us were experienced in stablecoin or crypto infra before working on Versine but our distributed systems experience has helped us a lot. We'd love for you guys to try it! It's available on iOS and Android and as an MCP on ChatGPT and Claude. We also support a public MCP and REST API for other agents. Please let us know how you find it and if it works as you'd hoped! Https://versine. Com Comments URL: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=50634426 Points: 65 # Comments: 47
summary: Launch HN: Versine (YC F26) – MCP to send and receive money.

content:
Amazon is promoting a discounted subscription to Apple TV for U.S. customers who shop on its platform. The deal reduces the standard $14.99‑per‑month price to $6.99 per month for the first six months, amounting to $42 in total compared with the regular $90 cost for the same period. title: Sen. Mike Rounds proposes attaching FISA Section 702 to NDAA as deadline looms
content: Weeks before the end of the legislative session, some members of Congress are scrambling to reauthorize a controversial warrantless wiretapping authority, possibly by attaching it to a must-pass military spending bill. Sen. Mike Rounds (R-SD) told Politico that Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) could be attached to the National Defense Authorization Act. It's the latest in a grueling fight over a major spying rule that hasn't technically lapsed. "We don't have two weeks to work just on FISA," said Rounds, a member of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence. "But if it's amended onto the NDAA then you can mo …
summary: Some members of Congress are scrambling to reauthorize the controversial warrantless wiretapping authority known as Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act before the legislative session ends. Sen. Mike Rounds (R‑SD) said the provision could be attached to the National Defense Authorization Act.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang tells staff Trump's role in his rehiring is untrue
content:
Jensen Huang apologized to staff during his first all‑hands meeting since returning to Nvidia, according to Bloomberg, The New York Times, and The Handbasket’s Marisa Kabas. He said he was trying to distance himself from a narrative that the White House and tech leaders had helped him regain his position.

During the meeting, Huang reportedly called claims that President Donald Trump was directly involved in his reinstatement—an idea publicly promoted by Trump himself—“completely untrue.” He added, “Don’t think for a second politics played a role in the company. We are the most apolitical company,” according to Kabas.
summary: Jensen Huang apologized to Nvidia staff during his first all‑hands meeting since returning to the company. He said claims that President Donald Trump directly helped his reinstatement are “completely untrue” and asserted the company is apolitical.
author: The Verge

title: TikTok outage on Tuesday disrupts videos and search, resolves by late afternoon
content:
TikTok experienced a service disruption earlier on Tuesday, with videos, search results, favorites and other features failing to load as usual. The outage affected the For You feed on iPhone, search results on iOS, Android and the web, profile pages that displayed blank screens, and video links that did not work.

By about 3:45 PM ET the platform appeared to be functioning normally again. Downdetector recorded roughly 25,000 user reports of the issue at around 2:56 PM ET, adding to a series of outages reported over the past couple of weeks.
summary: TikTok experienced an outage on Tuesday that prevented videos, search results, favorites and other features from loading on iOS, Android and the web. The problem appeared to be resolved by about 3:45 PM ET after roughly 25,000 reports were logged on Downdetector.
author: The Verge

title: Take-Two issues DMCA takedown, shuts down Leonida GTA VI PC project
content:
Take‑Two Interactive issued a DMCA takedown notice today that forced the removal of “Leonida,” a fan‑run recompilation project for Grand Theft Auto VI. The effort, created by 15‑year‑old “NotRexed,” was intended to translate a leaked Xbox version of GTA VI so it could run natively on Windows.

The leak, posted earlier this week by leaker “Cyberleek,” included a full Xbox build of the game and several gameplay videos released over the summer. Following the leak, modders have accelerated attempts to reverse‑engineer the code and rebuild it for PC, but the Leonida project has now been shut down.
summary: Take-Two sent a DMCA takedown notice that caused the Leonida fan project, created by 15‑year‑old “NotRexed,” to disappear. Leonida was intended to translate a leaked GTA VI Xbox build to run natively on Windows.
author: The Verge

title: US Army to Detonate 9,700 Pounds of Lead Azide at Iowa Ammunition Plant
content:
The U.S. Army is proceeding with a planned detonation of its lead azide stockpile at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa. The explosion is scheduled for approximately 9:00 AM Central Standard Time on Wednesday. A sign identifying the facility is visible inside the fence surrounding the plant, as captured in a Getty Images photo on November 19.

The material to be detonated consists of 68 drums containing roughly 9,700 pounds of lead azide, an unstable chemical compound used to initiate munitions such as grenades. Lead azide has been employed by the U.S. military as a primary explosive for nearly a century. About fifteen years ago, the Army began moving away from the compound because of the challenges associated with storing and transporting it, according to expert Robert Cekada.
summary: The US Army plans to detonate about 9,700 pounds of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa. The detonation is scheduled for 9:00 AM CST on Wednesday.
author: The Verge

title: FinCEN Investigates Cybersecurity Incident with Unauthorized System Access
content:
The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), a bureau within the Treasury Department, announced on Tuesday that it is investigating a “cybersecurity incident” that led to unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems. FinCEN did not disclose the full scope or source of the breach but said it has taken some systems offline as a precautionary measure.

The disclosure follows a report by The New York Times that the Central Intelligence Agency and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence had identified a breach of an open‑source intelligence system, exposing unclassified information.
summary: FinCEN, part of the Treasury Department, disclosed it is investigating a cybersecurity incident that caused unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems. The bureau has taken some systems offline as a precaution and has not released details on the scope or source of the breach.
author: The Verge

title: Kalshi pauses Utah trading after losing court battles
content:
Kalshi announced that it is pausing its operations in Utah after a series of court defeats, spokesperson Jacki McGavick said Monday. The company lost a legal effort to block Utah’s ongoing enforcement actions under the state’s gambling statutes.

The decision comes as multiple lawsuits in Utah continue to proceed, and Kalshi’s request to a federal appeals court to stay those cases pending an appeal was rejected. An emergency motion filed by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, which maintains that it has exclusive jurisdiction over prediction‑market trading, also did not prevent Utah’s enforcement actions, and a federal district court has not granted that motion.
summary: Kalshi made the “difficult decision” to pause operations in Utah after losing a court fight to block the state’s ongoing enforcement actions under Utah gambling laws, Kalshi spokesperson Jacki McGavick said Monday. It seems Kalshi’s legal troubles in Utah have become too much for the prediction market platform to gamble on continued operations there.
author: Ars Technica

title: OSU study shows timing and amount of smoke‑tainted hops key to beer quality
content:
Oregon State University scientists have investigated how brewers can mitigate the effects of smoke‑tainted hops that resulted from the 2020 wildfires, which burned over one million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the region and adversely affected hops grown for beer brewing, a crop that supplies more than 95 percent of U.S. hops and about 40 percent of the global supply.

In a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists, the researchers found that the impact of smoke‑tainted hops depends on both the quantity of affected hops used and the timing of their addition during the brewing process. The study suggests that brewers can still incorporate these hops while reducing negative flavor contributions.

Thomas Shellhammer, an OSU chemist who co‑authored the paper, previously identified the growing popularity of dry hopping—adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales—as a likely cause of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon.
summary: OSU scientists found that the protection of beers from smoke‑tainted hops depends on the amount of affected hops used and when they are added during brewing. The findings were published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists and co‑authored by OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer.
author: Ars Technica

title: Amazon Leo adds 36 satellites via Ariane 6 after Vulcan failure, speeds up Falcon 9 launches
content:
Amazon’s Leo broadband constellation has received a significant boost after a European Ariane 6 launch carried 36 satellites into orbit on Tuesday. The launch followed the loss of 40 satellites earlier this month when United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket failed, leaving Amazon’s primary launch provider grounded. With the Ariane 6 flight, the Amazon Leo fleet now totals 432 satellites, a key step in filling the gap left by the Vulcan outage.

In a statement to Ars, an Amazon official announced that the company is accelerating several Falcon 9 launches it has purchased from SpaceX. SpaceX also operates the Starlink satellite network, which Amazon aims to surpass. The next Falcon 9 launch for Amazon Leo is now scheduled for December, a date moved forward from the previous plan for next year.

Following the December flight, Amazon has several additional Falcon 9 missions planned to deploy Leo satellites in rapid succession, further expanding the constellation’s coverage.
summary: A European Ariane 6 launch placed 36 satellites into orbit for Amazon's Leo broadband constellation, bringing the fleet to 432 satellites after 40 were lost in a United Launch Alliance Vulcan failure. Amazon said it is accelerating Falcon 9 launches, moving the next flight to December and scheduling additional Falcon 9 missions in rapid succession.
author: Ars Technica

title: Amazon drone crashes onto Michigan garage after delivering shampoo, FAA investigates
content: An Amazon delivery drone that clipped a fiber-optic line before crashing onto a garage roof is now the subject of an investigation by the US Federal Aviation Administration. It’s the latest delivery drone mishap caught on video as Amazon and other companies are ramping up such aerial delivery operations across the United States. The November 20 incident began with Jim Brennan and his wife, residents of Huntington Woods, Michigan, placing an order for shampoo and being surprised by a notification about the package arriving by drone within seven minutes, according to WXYZ 7 News Detroit. After the drone dropped the package into Brennan’s backyard, it lost a propeller when it caught on fiber-optic cable and floundered sideways before getting pinned between the neighbor’s garage roof and some power lines. “Like a sick bird, it tried to go up, it tried to get out of here,” Brennan told WXYZ 7. Read full article Comments
summary: On November 20, an Amazon delivery drone clipped a fiber‑optic line and crashed onto a garage roof in Huntington Woods, Michigan after dropping a shampoo package for Jim Brennan and his wife. The crash, which left the drone pinned between the garage and power lines, is now being investigated by the US Federal Aviation Administration.
author: Ars Technica

title: Mathematician uses AI to produce proof of Riemann hypothesis
content:
Last week a report emerged that a mathematician employed artificial‑intelligence tools to produce a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics’ most celebrated open problems. The announcement follows a series of recent breakthroughs in the discipline that have been either facilitated by or wholly generated with large‑language‑model systems, a development that has unsettled many researchers in the field.

The Riemann hypothesis, first formulated by Bernhard Riemann in the mid‑1800s, concerns the distribution of prime numbers and underpins work in number theory and cryptography. Wikipedia describes it as “one of the most important problems in the field” of pure mathematics. While the proof itself has not yet been examined in detail, mathematicians are currently reviewing the claim and assessing its implications for the broader mathematical community.
summary: A mathematician announced a proof of the Riemann hypothesis that was aided by artificial intelligence. Researchers are currently examining the proof and its implications.
author: Ars Technica

title: Microsoft declares “Code Red” overhaul after historic November 12 cloud outage
content:
Microsoft has launched a “Code Red” overhaul of its engineering response practices after a November 12 outage that blocked access to Exchange Online, Teams and Outlook for users worldwide. Internal memos reviewed by Reuters show Microsoft 365 Core President Jason Henderson calling the incident the greatest customer impact in Exchange Online’s history. Henderson also noted that an urgent production fix in a recent incident required five to six days to achieve worldwide saturation, while the company’s goal for its most urgent security fixes is to move from detection to safe worldwide deployment within one hour—a target it has not yet met.

A post‑incident report dated November 20 attributes the downtime to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July, which created lock contention in gateway processes. A Teams traffic failover then added extra load to infrastructure already strained, because maintenance had left roughly 14 percent of gateway server capacity offline at the time of the incident. The memos outlining these findings have not been published by Microsoft.
summary: Microsoft declares “Code Red” overhaul after historic November 12 cloud outage.
author: Ars Technica

title: NASA suspends science on Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter due to technical issues
content:
Two of NASA’s four active Mars missions have temporarily halted science operations after encountering separate technical problems. The affected spacecraft are the Perseverance rover and the Odyssey orbiter, both of which are operating beyond their original design lifetimes.

Perseverance, now in its sixth year on the Martian surface, has been gathering rock and soil samples for a future return to Earth and is currently studying the rim of a crater that once held an ancient lake. The rover’s outage is linked to its communications system, which includes two redundant UHF radios for high‑rate links to orbiters and a separate X‑band antenna for lower‑rate direct‑to‑Earth transmissions.

Odyssey, launched in 2001 and the longest‑living Mars mission, is also offline for science work while its technical issue is addressed. Both suspensions are described as hopefully temporary.
summary: Two of NASA's four Mars missions, the Perseverance rover and the Odyssey orbiter, have suspended science operations because of separate technical issues. Both spacecraft are operating beyond their original design lifetimes, with Perseverance in its sixth year studying a crater rim and Odyssey, launched in 2001, being the longest-lived Mars mission.
author: Ars Technica

title: New benchmark shows top AI agents struggle with everyday tasks
content: A new benchmark shows that, despite widespread use of personal AI assistants, even the most advanced AI models have difficulty completing everyday tasks reliably and safely, and may introduce new problems. The findings highlight ongoing limitations in current AI agents’ everyday performance.
summary: Millions are adopting personal AI assistants. A new benchmark reveals that even the most advanced AI models fail to complete everyday tasks reliably and safely without creating potential new problems.

title: Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld warns Nvidia harms U.S. industrial might
content: Yale professor Jeffrey Sonnenfeld cautioned that the market’s enthusiasm on Monday for Jensen Huang’s White House‑backed return as Nvidia’s chief executive and board member may be a serious error. Sonnenfeld said the move could expose Nvidia’s directors to “historic” personal liability amid an expanding slate of lawsuits. He also questioned whether the United States should celebrate a company that, in his view, has contributed advanced chips to adversary nations, suggesting Nvidia may be a detriment rather than a champion of U.S. industrial strength.
summary: Sonnenfeld cautioned that Jensen Huang's White House‑backed return as Nvidia CEO and board member could be a major mistake. He said the move may expose directors to historic personal liability and questioned celebrating a company that supplies advanced chips to adversaries.
author: TechCrunch

title: Tech stocks retreat as Nvidia falls 6% after Jensen Huang's return
content:
Technology shares led a market retreat on Tuesday, as investors braced for further volatility in the AI sector that drives global economic growth. The sell‑off followed a return of Jensen Huang to the CEO position at Nvidia, days after he had been forced to resign.  

A day after Huang’s reinstatement sent Nvidia shares up more than 30% and added over $900 billion to the company’s market value, the euphoria faded. By the close of trading on Tuesday, Nvidia’s stock had fallen almost 6%, marking a sharp reversal of the earlier rally.
summary: Technology shares led a market retreat on Tuesday as investors grew cautious after Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia’s CEO days after his forced resignation. Nvidia’s stock, which had risen more than 30% and added over $900 billion in market value after his return, slipped almost 6% by Tuesday’s close.
author: Guardian Technology

content: The United States and Armenia have launched the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP), a regional transit initiative that has entered construction. title: Istanbul lioness sighting prompts search, authorities say no big cat found
content: Reports of a lioness roaming north of Istanbul triggered a security scramble after grainy footage appeared to show a large cat prowling across open land. After a day of searches, Turkish authorities confirmed that the animal was neither a lion nor any other big cat.
summary: Grainy footage that appeared to show a lioness roaming north of Istanbul led Turkish authorities to launch a large search. After a day of searching, officials said the animal was not a lion or any other big cat.

title: Sixteen chefs vie for world egg mayonnaise champion title in Saint-Ouen
content: Sixteen finalists gathered near Paris to vie for the world egg mayonnaise championship, held in Saint‑Ouen just outside the city on Monday, 23 November 2026. The event celebrates a deceptively simple French bistro classic that demands considerable culinary skill.

title: Rosstat leak shows at least 490,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine
content: A data leak from Russia’s statistics agency, Rosstat, shows that at least 490,000 Russian soldiers have died in Ukraine. The figure was extracted by two hacking groups on 1 November from death certificates recorded up to the end of August, excluding missing servicemen and deaths not yet documented.
summary: Two hacking groups extracted the data from Rosstat on 1 November. The figure, based on death certificates registered through August, shows at least 490,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine and excludes missing servicemen and deaths not yet recorded.

content:
François Picard welcomed Andrew Weissmann, a Professor of Practice at NYU School of Law and former federal prosecutor noted for leading major DOJ and FBI investigations. Picard asked, “Why were they treating Nvidia so favorably?” to set the tone for the discussion.  

Weissmann will examine the legal and ethical questions surrounding the Trump administration’s dealings with the chipmaker. He will address allegations of personal financial gain, the implications for U.S. national security, the limits of presidential immunity, and what he calls an “unholy alliance of tech bros, of Wall Street, and of politicians.”
summary: Nvidia Allegations: Trump Administration Favorable Treatment and Pay‑to‑Play Claims.

title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia comeback sends AI videos into overdrive
content: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia as CEO 11 days after his resignation, prompting a surge of AI‑generated videos that reference his comeback. The online response shifted from last week’s memes that mocked him to a wave of celebratory content. A viral clip that appeared to show Huang dancing was identified as AI‑manipulated footage of a basketball coach from 2016. According to Vedika Bahl, the AI technology Nvidia helped popularise is now reshaping the narrative surrounding its chief executive.
summary: Just 11 days after resigning as Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang’s return has unleashed a fresh wave of AI-generated videos. But the internet has changed its tune: while last week’s memes mocked Huang, many now celebrate his comeback.
author: France 24

title: Trump reinstates Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, prompting congressional and judicial scrutiny
content:
Angela Diffley welcomed Bernard Benhamou, Secretary General of the Institute of Digital Sovereignty and Senior Lecturer in Internet Governance at Paris 1 Panthéon‑Sorbonne University.  

Benhamou discussed Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, asking what it means for Trump, Lutnick, the US, the AI industry and China. He called Huang “the global banker of the AI industry” and said, “He is the visionary, he is the banker. He's not only the chip maker.”  

Benhamou warned that Donald Trump’s decision to reinstate the Nvidia CEO could bring congressional and judicial scrutiny. He added, “It’s far from over. It’s just the beginning.”
summary: Angela Diffley welcomed Bernard Benhamou, Secretary General of the Institute of Digital Sovereignty and Senior Lecturer in Internet Governance at Paris 1 Panthéon‑Sorbonne University. Benhamou warned that Donald Trump’s decision to reinstate Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang could bring congressional and judicial scrutiny.

content:
After a ten‑week trial, a 12‑person jury has begun deliberations in the double‑murder case against former police officer Beau Lamarre‑Condon. The jurors will decide whether Lamar‑Condon is responsible for the deaths of Jesse Baird and his new partner, Luke Davies.

Prosecutors allege that Lamar‑Condon used his police service weapon to fatally shoot Baird and Davies inside Baird’s home in Paddington on 19 February 2024. The verdict now rests with the jury.

title: Australia inflation rises to 4.9% in year to October, up from 4.3%
content:
Inflation in Australia rose to 4.9 % in the year to October, up from 4.3 % in September. The increase brings the rate nearly double the Reserve Bank of Australia’s official target of 2.5 %.

The rise is driven by surging fuel costs, which jumped 6.3 % last month, and the removal of electricity rebates. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, electricity prices were 25 % higher than a year earlier, adding to cost‑of‑living pressures that peak ahead of Christmas.
summary: Australia inflation rises to 4.9% in year to October, up from 4.3%.

title: China launching 1st international astronaut to Tiangong space station today: Watch it live
content:
China is set to launch its first international astronaut to the Tiangong space station on November 24, marking a historic milestone for the nation’s space program. The Shenzhou-24 mission will lift off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China at 7:18 p.m. EST (8:18 a.m. Beijing time on November 25) aboard a Long March 2F rocket. This flight represents China’s 18th crewed spaceflight and its 12th mission to the three-module Tiangong station, which was completed in low Earth orbit in late 2022.

The crew includes commander Tang Hongbo, flight engineer Wu Yi, and payload specialist Muhammad Zeeshan Ali. Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan’s armed forces, will be the first person from his country to reach orbit. His selection followed a spaceflight cooperation agreement signed between China and Pakistan in February 2025, after which two Pakistani candidates traveled to China for training. China announced the final crew on November 23, consistent with its practice of revealing astronaut identities only the day before launch.

Tang Hongbo, who previously flew on the Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 missions, will become the first person to visit Tiangong three times. Wu Yi is embarking on her first spaceflight. While Tang and Wu are expected to remain aboard the station for the standard six-month rotation, Ali will stay in orbit for approximately one week. He will return to Earth with Zhang Zhiyuan and Lai Ka-ying of the Shenzhou-23 mission, which launched on May 24.

The Shenzhou-23 crewmate Zhu Yangzhu will remain on Tiangong after Ali’s departure, staying until the Shenzhou-24 crew returns. This arrangement will make Zhu the first Chinese astronaut to spend a year in orbit, a milestone intended to prepare China for future long-duration missions to the moon and other deep-space destinations.
summary: China will send an international astronaut to its Tiangong space station today (Nov. 24) for the first time ever, and you can watch the landmark liftoff live.
author: Space.com

title: YunLone Galaxy Projector review: $28 star light offers app control and aurora effects
content:
The YunLone Galaxy Projector is a star projector priced at approximately $28, designed to display aurora-style light patterns on walls and ceilings. The device measures 3.54 by 3.15 by 4.72 inches and weighs 17.6 ounces. It features an LED bulb, a laser, a built-in speaker, and a sleep timer. Operation is supported by both a companion app and a remote control, and the unit includes rotation capabilities. The manufacturer describes the product as a customizable night light intended for creating a relaxing atmosphere in living rooms or bedrooms.

The design of the YunLone Galaxy Projector prioritizes functionality over aesthetics. It has a circular shape with a clear globe in the center that serves as the projector. The unit sits on rubberized feet to prevent slipping and is naturally tilted to point slightly diagonally, which helps spread the lights across the room. The build quality is described as sturdy, made from hard-wearing plastic that is suitable for use in a child’s bedroom. The front of the unit has limited buttons, and the overall appearance is basic rather than decorative.

In terms of performance, the projector displays colorful, dancing auroras rather than accurate scientific constellations or close-ups of the moon. Users can control the projection via an app for Android or Apple smartphones, allowing for extensive customization. The app offers preset arrangements labeled by seasons, colors, or holidays, as well as a color wheel for creating custom schemes. Users can also adjust brightness, enable a "breathing" effect, and control the speed of the ripples. A laser feature projects green stars, which can be turned off independently or adjusted for brightness. The projection has a wide reach, covering most of the walls and ceiling in the test bedroom.

Functionality includes a Bluetooth speaker with decent audio quality, suitable for audiobooks and podcasts, though it lacks significant bass. The device also contains eight built-in sound effects, such as white noise, waves, lullabies, and a storm. While the app provides superior control, the bundled remote control, which requires two AAA batteries, offers more limited options for setting basic colors and speeds. The pairing process with the app is noted as not being entirely straightforward, requiring the user to quickly turn the unit on and off three times to enter pairing mode, which may take several attempts.

The review concludes that the YunLone Galaxy Projector is a strong option for those seeking a budget-friendly, non-scientific projector for relaxation. For users interested in accurate astronomical projections, the review suggests alternatives such as the Sega Toys Homestar Classic or the Hommkiety Galaxy Projector. The Sega Toys range offers excellent projections but comes with a higher price tag and requires purchasing extra discs for different images. The Hommkiety Galaxy Projector, priced closer to $50, includes several interchangeable discs in the box for displaying various space images.
summary: The YunLone Galaxy Projector costs around $28 and features a laser, Bluetooth speaker, and app support for extensive color customization. Reviewers describe it as a sturdy, functional unit that projects wide-reaching aurora patterns, though it does not display accurate scientific constellations.
author: Space.com

title: Joe Biden memoir defends decisions, blames party for re-election loss
content: New memoir tells of policy feats and battles with Trump but struggles to take responsibility for re-election debacle Inevitably, readers of Joe Biden’s new memoir will flick forward to find what he says about the events that ended his presidency: increasing pressure about his age and capacity that finally led him to stand aside and anoint Kamala Harris, too late, ushering fascism back to the White House. Alas, Biden thinks he was just fine to keep on serving and the whole thing was a stitch-up by a panicked party. Of his catastrophic debate in June 2024, when the then 81-year-old president blinked, stuttered and gaped under the lights, Biden writes: “I knew the debate had gone badly. But I knew that debates had gone badly for lots of incumbent presidents. Especially their first ones. I left the stage thinking I would be debating Trump once more before the election was over. I was wrong. This wasn’t just the first debate, it was my last one.” He raises Barack Obama’s poor performance in his first debate with Mitt Romney in 2012, when Biden was VP. Caught cold, Obama prepared for the next one and cruised to re-election.
summary: Joe Biden’s new memoir details his policy achievements and conflicts with Trump while arguing that his withdrawal from the presidential race was forced by a panicked party. The book defends his performance in the June 2024 debate by comparing it to Barack Obama’s poor first debate in 2012.

title: Photographer Robert Nickelsberg documents 20 years of trauma in Kashmir
content: Photographer Robert Nickelsberg has documented the Kashmiri people’s plight for over 20 years. His images illustrate how trauma has become integrated into the region’s everyday life, highlighting themes of grief, fear, and resilience.
summary: Robert Nickelsberg has photographed the plight of Kashmiri people for more than 20 years. His images reveal how trauma has settled into the fabric of everyday life.

title: From Sovereigns to Servants by Alexandra Prokopenko review – Putin and his yes men
content: A disturbing account of the way Russia’s elites have reduced themselves to craven courtiers When Vladimir Putin launched his full-scale invasion of Ukraine four and a half years ago, it was a shock, but it wasn’t a surprise. The US and the UK had been publicly warning their allies for weeks about what Russia was planning, as well as threatening the Russians with a wave of sanctions unprecedented against a major power. Putin’s foreign policy had long relied on confusion and untruth. By saying that they knew exactly what he was up to, Britain and America were hoping first to deny him his usual ambiguity, and second to pressure the men around him into making him stop, since war would deprive them of the stolen assets they’d stashed in London’s most exclusive neighbourhoods.
summary: The review describes Alexandra Prokopenko’s book as a disturbing account of Russia’s elites reducing themselves to craven courtiers. It notes that Putin’s full‑scale invasion of Ukraine began four and a half years ago and that the US and UK warned allies and threatened unprecedented sanctions to pressure those around him.

title: Only 3.8% of GTA VI reviewers were women despite female protagonist
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI has emerged as the biggest video game launch of all time, breaking sales and streaming records to become the best-reviewed game ever, surpassing 1998’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. The release is described as a once-in-a-lifetime phenomenon that will shape the gaming medium and pop culture for years, occurring while developers at studio Rockstar Games fight for their rights. Notably, this is the first Grand Theft Auto title in thirty years to feature a female protagonist, who is also a woman of colour.

Despite the game’s cultural significance and its historic lead character, very few women reviewed the title before its release. When the review embargo lifted on 18 November, a stark gender imbalance was evident among the 156 reviewers, with only six appearing to be women. This represents just 3.8% of the total, a statistic highlighted by journalist Lex Luddy in a BlueSky post. The source notes that seemingly no women of colour participated in the pre-release reviews, creating a contrast between the game’s inclusive protagonist and the demographic of its critical reception.
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI became the best-reviewed game ever and the biggest video game launch of all time. Despite featuring the first female protagonist in the series, only six of 156 pre-release reviewers appeared to be women.
author: Guardian Culture

title: GTA VI becomes largest video game release with 364.5m streaming hours
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI recently became the largest video game release of all time, with current estimates indicating that at least 30 million people are playing the title. The game’s launch has generated significant engagement from content creators, who have produced hundreds of millions of hours of video content since its release.

According to streaming data from analytics company Streams Charts, a cumulative 364.5 million hours of the game were watched within just two days of its launch. This volume of viewing time is equivalent to roughly 41,000 years of content. The data highlights the massive scale of audience interest in Rockstar Game’s long-awaited title, translating the total watch time into activities such as rifling through cash registers, hanging drywall, birding, diving, or hijacking jets.
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI became the largest video game release of all time, with current estimates indicating at least 30 million players. Streaming data from Streams Charts shows a cumulative 364.5 million hours were watched within two days of its release.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Robert Pattinson cast as James Bond in Denis Villeneuve's Amazon film
content:
Robert Pattinson has been officially cast as James Bond for a new Amazon-produced film directed by Denis Villeneuve. While no release date has been confirmed, fall 2028 appears to be a likely target, aligning with the release schedules of previous Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig installments. This casting decision has sparked speculation regarding who will be selected for the role of the Bond girl in the rebooted installment.

The article notes that Pattinson’s fame predates his Bond role, distinguishing him from previous actors who gained recognition through the franchise. His extensive filmography includes work with directors such as David Cronenberg, Claire Denis, and Lance Oppenheim, as well as appearances in Twilight, Batman, and Christopher Nolan movies. This shift in the typical casting trajectory has inspired predictions that a similarly high-profile actress, such as Sydney Sweeney, could be chosen for the supporting role.
summary: Robert Pattinson has been officially cast as James Bond for a new Amazon-produced film directed by Denis Villeneuve, with a likely release target of fall 2028. Speculation has begun regarding who will be cast as the Bond girl, with some suggesting Sydney Sweeney for the role.

title: Review: Disney's Hexed is a witchy caper and a wicked disappointment
content:
Disney’s new animated film, Hexed, has been criticized as a "wicked disappointment" that fails to deliver on its witchy premise. The review describes the movie, which centers on a teenage girl discovering her magical heritage, as a "mostly magic-free" experience that highlights the studio’s struggles with original storytelling. The article argues that Disney’s recent original output, including titles like Elio, Strange World, and Wish, has felt uninspired and unoriginal.

The piece specifically notes that Wish, released three Thanksgivings ago, was Disney’s worst-reviewed animated film in almost two decades and resulted in a box office failure that cost approximately $131 million. Despite this setback, the review states that the film’s co-director, Fawn Veerasunthorn, who previously worked with Moana 2 director Jason Hand, is returning this holiday season with Hexed. The reviewer characterizes the new film as a "rote rip-off adventure" that does not deserve its place in the Disney franchise lineup.
summary: The film follows a teen girl who discovers she is a witch in a story described as mostly magic-free. The review argues the movie is a rote rip-off that highlights the uninspired state of Disney's original animation.

title: Philippe Diallo faces uphill battle against Infantino in March Fifa election
content:
Philippe Diallo, the French Football president, is facing significant difficulties in securing support for his challenge to Gianni Infantino ahead of the March Fifa election. At the Confederation of African Football (Caf) general assembly last weekend, Diallo attended as a guest and was subjected to an uncomfortable moment when Caf president Patrice Motsepe requested that the presidents and general secretaries of the 54 member associations give Infantino a standing ovation.

This incident highlights the uphill battle Diallo faces in winning the backing of the continent’s decision-makers. The article suggests that the campaign to displace Infantino from the Fifa presidency is a harsh and unforgiving endeavor, with Diallo quickly learning the realities of this global political challenge.
summary: French Football president Philippe Diallo is facing difficulty in securing support from African decision-makers for the March Fifa election. He recently had to endure a standing ovation for incumbent president Gianni Infantino during a Caf general assembly.

title: UK nations await Fifa decision on 2035 Women's World Cup automatic entry
content:
England, Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales remain uncertain about whether they will receive automatic qualification for the 2035 Women’s World Cup as hosts. While the four 2031 hosts have already been granted automatic places, domestic Football Associations have not yet been informed of the specific qualification plans for the 2035 tournament following the formal acceptance of their bid.

Fifa is set to make the final decision on the qualifying procedures. Sources at the domestic Football Associations told the Guardian that they are still in the dark regarding their status, highlighting a gap in communication between the governing body and the host nations.
summary: England, Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales are uncertain if they will receive automatic qualification for the 2035 Women's World Cup. Fifa will determine the qualifying procedures, and domestic Football Associations have not yet been informed of the plan.

content: Youngest title match in chess history starts Tuesday Sindarov and Gukesh open Game 1 with Berlin defense Explainer: all your pre-match questions, answered Preview: Gukesh vows to win title ‘all over again’ Sindarov interview: ‘I can’t play games just for fun’ Play through 22 famous world championship games Bluesky Bryan at @BryanAGraham or email him The players have shaken hands and we’re off! title: Senegal restored as Africa Cup of Nations champions after CAS ruling
content:
Senegal has been restored as Africa Cup of Nations champions after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS). The decision reversed a March appeals panel ruling that had awarded Morocco a 3‑0 default win. The CAS ruling reinstated Senegal’s 1‑0 victory.

The original final, played in January, saw Senegal beat Morocco 1‑0 after the Moroccan side walked off the pitch. The CAF‑appointed appeals panel later overturned the result, awarding Morocco a 3‑0 win, before CAS reversed the decision.
summary: Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations champions following a Court of Arbitration for Sport decision. The ruling reverses a March overturn that had awarded a 3‑0 win to Morocco after Senegal’s 1‑0 victory in the January final was reversed by a CAF appeals panel.

title: Sen. Deb Fischer announces death of husband Bruce
content: Senate Republican Deb Fischer of Nebraska announced that her husband, Bruce, has died. She posted the news on the social platform X, describing him as her “partner in life” and her “greatest source of strength.” Fischer said she shared the passing with a heavy heart.
summary: Sen. Deb Fischer announces death of husband Bruce.

title: Trump to Award Giuliani Presidential Medal of Freedom on Tuesday
content: President Trump will present the Presidential Medal of Freedom to former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani (R) on Tuesday. Giuliani, 82, confirmed the award during a Monday appearance on Steve Bannon’s “War Room” podcast, noting it follows more than a year after he announced plans to bestow the nation’s highest civilian honor on his longtime ally.
summary: President Trump will award former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani the Presidential Medal of Freedom on Tuesday. Giuliani, 82, announced the award during a Monday appearance on Steve Bannon’s “War Room” podcast.

title: Trump Shares Meme of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with Blood on Face
content: President Trump posted a meme on Truth Social on Monday celebrating the return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The image, which appears to be AI‑generated, depicts Huang with blood on his face and a fist raised in the air, echoing a famous photo of Trump after the 2024 Butler, Pa. incident.
summary: President Trump posted a meme on Truth Social Monday celebrating the return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The AI‑generated photo shows Huang with blood on his face and a fist in the air, riffing on a famous image of Trump after his attempted 2024 assassination in Butler, Pa.

title: Nvidia Reinstates Co-Founder Jensen Huang as CEO After Resignation Over Affairs
content:
Nvidia co‑founder Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO on Monday after the board reversed his resignation. Huang had stepped down following admissions of affairs with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence and a subordinate. He returned to the company’s headquarters to cheers.  

The headline also notes the Army’s Iowa lead detonation, though no further details are provided in the article.
summary: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO on Monday after resigning following admissions of affairs. The board reversed the decision amid reports that the affairs involved a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence and a subordinate.

title: House Democrat Demands Public Hearing from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
content: A ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee called on Tuesday for a public hearing with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The request comes amid growing scrutiny of Huang following reports of a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. The lawmaker stated that the American people deserve to hear publicly from Huang regarding how potentially billions of dollars are involved.
summary: A ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee called for a public hearing with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who was recently reinstated. Huang has been facing scrutiny over reports of a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.

title: Trump awards Giuliani Medal of Freedom
content: President Trump awarded former New York Mayor Rudy Giuliani the Medal of Freedom, the nation’s highest civilian honor, on Tuesday. The citation recognized Giuliani’s actions following the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, which earned him the nickname “America’s Mayor.” A White House official described him as “one of the greatest leaders in New York.”

content: The Conservative Party has accused Andy Burnham of turning Number 10 into a "joke" following a controversy involving social media influencer Max Balegde. Balegde recently deleted a TikTok video filmed outside the Number 10 door, in which he mimed along to explicit lyrics.

content: Discover and buy more of Ben’s cartoons here Order your own print of this cartoon from the Guardian Print Shop Ben’s latest book, Drawn to the Chaos, is available to order now
